name: curl
summary: A portable transfer library and command-line tool whose libcurl API models transfers with reusable easy handles, multi-handle coordination, connection reuse, and protocol-specific nonblocking state machines.

features.name: Transfer-oriented reusable easy handle
features.description: libcurl represents an individual transfer with an opaque easy handle whose options configure the transfer and whose callbacks deliver or consume data. Easy handles can be reused after completion, with options remaining set until changed or reset.
benefits: Presents one stable application boundary across supported protocols
Allows transfer configuration and reuse without exposing protocol internals
costs: Sticky options and deferred validation require careful handle lifecycle management
Protocol-specific behavior remains behind a broad and option-rich API

features.name: Multi-handle event coordination
features.description: The multi interface groups one or more easy handles and lets an application drive nonblocking progress using sockets, timeouts, and repeated perform calls. Completion messages identify finished transfers, while adding or removing handles changes the active transfer set.
benefits: Supports multiple transfers in one application event loop
Allows applications to integrate transfer readiness with their own file descriptors
costs: The application must drive readiness, timeout, and completion processing correctly
Adding and removing handles changes transfer ownership and can abort active work

features.name: Protocol and transfer state machines
features.description: curl's transfer engine advances nonblocking state machines as data and socket readiness become available. Each transfer has a main mode state, and protocol handlers may add protocol-specific states and socket-interest calculations.
benefits: Preserves progress across partial network operations
Separates generic transfer orchestration from protocol-specific behavior
costs: State-space growth makes protocol and error-path reasoning substantial
Each protocol must preserve progress and readiness contracts across callbacks

features.name: Connection cache and multiplexing boundary
features.description: libcurl separates transfer-specific state from connection state and can reuse connections through a connection cache. Multiple easy handles may be associated with streams sharing a connection when protocol multiplexing is available.
benefits: Avoids repeating connection setup when reuse is possible
Separates per-transfer state from reusable transport state
costs: Connection ownership and transfer association require precise lifecycle rules
Multiplexing introduces additional scheduling and stream-state interactions

mathematical_views.question: How does an individual transfer progress from setup through connection, protocol work, data transfer, and completion?
assumptions: A transfer has a finite set of implementation-defined modes and transitions
Readiness, timeout, protocol results, and errors are transition inputs
The view abstracts individual protocol wire formats and platform socket APIs

mathematical_views.question: How are multiple transfer handles coordinated and reported through a multi handle?
assumptions: A multi handle is a coordinator vertex and easy handles are transfer vertices
Membership edges determine which transfers are driven together
Completion messages represent terminal observations rather than proof of application-level success

mathematical_views.question: Which transfer-specific states may share reusable connection state?
assumptions: Transfers and connections are distinct vertices with association edges
A connection may be reused only when protocol and lifecycle conditions permit
The view abstracts the detailed connection-cache eviction policy and wire protocol rules

benefits: Portable transfer configuration and callback boundary
costs: Option persistence and broad protocol surface complicate lifecycle reasoning
Readiness, timeout, and completion driving become application responsibilities

benefits: Nonblocking progress across partial protocol operations
costs: Many protocol and failure transitions increase implementation complexity

benefits: Connection reuse can reduce repeated setup work
costs: Shared transport state increases association and scheduling complexity
